brief.headline: Memory stocks rally on Temasek reports; HBM3E pricing holds, CoWoS gap narrows to 10% by YE26
brief.summary: <cite index="40-1,41-1,41-4">Samsung and SK Hynix surged 6.7% and 5.5% respectively on Aug 12 after reports that Singapore's Temasek plans direct investments in both chipmakers</cite>, <cite index="41-2">sending the KOSPI up 3.7%</cite>. <cite index="12-6,12-7">DDR4 spot prices hit $24 in July, up 14.3% MoM, while NAND climbed 4.3% to $30.1</cite>; <cite index="11-1">TrendForce projects Q3 contract DRAM +13-18% QoQ and NAND +10-15%</cite>, decelerating from Q2's 58-63% and 70-75% jumps. <cite index="5-3,5-7">SK Hynix maintains ~50% HBM market share in 2026 with only 'minimal to modest' HBM3E pricing downtick expected vs 2025</cite>. <cite index="21-2,21-6">Hyperscalers committed $660-690B capex in 2026, nearly doubling 2025</cite>, while <cite index="29-10">TSMC's CoWoS supply-demand gap is narrowing from 20% currently to ~10% by end-2026</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: Neutral to slight favor SK Hynix. <cite index="9-3">SK Hynix controlled 57% of Q4 2025 HBM revenue vs Samsung 22%</cite>, and <cite index="8-9">Hynix is the only supplier able to deliver both HBM3E and HBM4 at scale in 2026</cite>. Samsung faces ongoing HBM3E qualification delays (<cite index="5-4">Nvidia negotiations continue as Samsung inches closer to qualification</cite>). Both benefit from <cite index="8-11">BofA forecasts of +51% DRAM revenue and +45% NAND in 2026 with ASPs up 30%+</cite>. Temasek flow provides symmetric upside. Tactical edge to Hynix on HBM leadership and margin trajectory (<cite index="34-7">Bernstein projects Hynix DRAM gross margins peaking at ~92.7% in Q4 2026</cite>), but Samsung's diversified logic/foundry exposure limits relative downside if memory cycle turns.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="11-1">Q3 2026 contract price increases moderate to +13-18% DRAM and +10-15% NAND QoQ</cite>, down sharply from <cite index="16-2,16-7">Q2's +58-63% DRAM and +70-75% NAND</cite>. <cite index="11-4,11-5">Consumer demand softening as higher memory costs feed into retail pricing, pressuring PC shipments and smartphone production</cite>. <cite index="8-3,8-13">Top three memory makers have pre-sold full HBM output for 2026, with Micron guiding 68% gross margin in Q2 2026</cite>. <cite index="9-1,9-2">Memory shortages expected through 2027, giving suppliers stronger pricing power than historically typical</cite>. <cite index="11-9,11-10">Server/AI demand keeps supply constrained while capacity shifts to higher-margin products, leaving less for consumer memory</cite>. Cycle remains structurally supported by AI but rate-of-change decelerating; peak pricing likely H2 2026.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="5-6">HBM bit shipments projected to jump 35% in 2026 to 17.1B Gb</cite>. <cite index="8-2,8-3">HBM3E remains dominant AI memory through 2026 with pricing power intact; full capacity pre-sold</cite>. <cite index="5-7">Hynix expects only minimal-to-modest HBM3E downtick in 2026 vs 2025</cite> as <cite index="5-4">Samsung qualification progress and Nvidia negotiations introduce marginal pricing pressure</cite>. <cite index="1-5">Micron announced HBM3E 36GB 12-high integration into AMD Instinct MI350</cite>; <cite index="1-6,1-7">AMD MI400 features 12 HBM4 stacks (432GB, 19.6TB/s), each delivering ~1.6TB/s</cite>. <cite index="19-1,19-2">HBM sold only on confidential contracts with no spot market; HBM4 launches Q3 2026</cite>. Supply remains the binding constraint through 2027; Samsung's lag in qualification limits competitive relief for hyperscalers locked into Hynix/Micron allocations.

news_pulse.headline: Temasek plans direct Samsung, SK Hynix investments
news_pulse.implication: First direct Korean stock investment for $401B sovereign fund; 6% AI portfolio today, targeting 15% by 2031. Validates memory thesis at cycle highs; adds incremental technical bid but no fundamental change to HBM allocation or pricing.

news_pulse.headline: July DRAM prices hit $24, up 14.3% MoM; NAND $30.1, +4.3%
news_pulse.implication: 19 consecutive months of NAND increases; DDR4 up 8x since June 2016 baseline. Spot pricing confirms contract strength but deceleration vs Q2 pace (58-75% QoQ) signals incremental consumer demand destruction.

news_pulse.headline: TrendForce: Q3 DRAM +13-18% QoQ, NAND +10-15% QoQ
news_pulse.implication: Sequential deceleration from Q2 gains but still double-digit; server demand healthy through 2027, consumer inventories building. Pricing power intact but slope rolling over—supports margin sustainment thesis, not acceleration.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex $660-690B, up ~64% YoY
news_pulse.implication: Amazon $200B, Alphabet $175-185B, Meta $115-135B, Microsoft $120B+, Oracle $50B. All report supply-constrained environments. Underpins memory demand floor; GPU/HBM coupling means sustained allocations for Hynix/Samsung.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS gap narrows 20% → 10% by end-2026
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS capacity 115-140k wpm by YE26, 170k wpm in 2027; 80% CAGR 2022-27. Easing packaging bottleneck accelerates GPU shipments → higher HBM pull. Positive for Hynix/Samsung bit growth but also signals backend constraint relief reduces urgency premium in negotiations.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix 57% Q4 2025 HBM revenue share; Samsung 22%, Micron 21%
news_pulse.implication: Hynix dominance extends; reported 5x quarterly profit jump in April. Samsung qualification delays limit share gain despite capacity adds. Market structure remains oligopoly with Hynix pricing power through 2027.

news_pulse.headline: Morgan Stanley adds SpaceX to hyperscaler basket; 2027 capex $1.15T
news_pulse.implication: SpaceX $159B capex proj., $15.8B Q2 AI compute spend, targeting 2GW by YE26. Expands hyperscaler TAM beyond traditional cloud; incremental memory demand source but execution risk high and timing uncertain.

news_pulse.headline: ADATA warns Q3 DRAM +20-30%, NAND +35-40% contract price increases
news_pulse.implication: Module maker passing through upstream costs; shortages expected through 2028. Consumer pain point rising but LTAs with hyperscalers lock in volume. Bifurcated market: enterprise pays, consumer cuts back.

brief.derivatives_signal: No structured derivatives data in payload. Equity option flow likely skewed call-heavy on Temasek headline (both names +6-7% intraday). KOSPI 200 futures would have tracked index +3.7% move. Watch for gamma unwind if Temasek denies or clarifies scope; funds may have front-run allocations. ADRs (SSNLF, HXSCL) gapped on US session follow-through. Implied vol likely compressed post-rally; any pullback sets up vol expansion into earnings windows (Samsung likely late-Oct, Hynix early-Oct based on historical). Pair trade: long Hynix vol vs short Samsung vol on HBM qualification binary.
